1. Manually screw all screws, bolts and/or nuts.
2. Apply half the recommended torque value.
3. 11ghten fastener to the recommended torque value.

NOTE: When possible, always apply torque on the nut.
NOTE: Always torque screws, bolts and/or nuts using a crisscross pattern when multiple fasteners are
used to secure a part (eg. a cylinder head). Some parts must be torqued according toa specific sequence
and torque pattern as detailed in the installation procedure.

When the engine is running and there is no shift selected, oil is supplied from the oil tank to the HCM
oil pump.
Oil is then circulated through a passageway in the clutch solenoid back through the HCM oil pump in a
continuous loop to maintain the oil flow ready for any upcoming shift request.

Subsection O2 (CONTROLLER AREA NETWORK (CAN))
CONTROLLER AREA NETWORK (CAN)
GENERAL
SYSTEM DESCRIPTION
The CAN (Controller Area Network) protocol is an ISO standard for serial data communication. The CAN
bus links several electronic modules (ECU's) and sensors in the vehicle. 2 wires connect each compo-
nent and they are in constant communication with each other at a rate of about every 20 milliseconds.
CAN lines consist of a pair of wires (WHITE/BEIGE and WHITE/BLACK).
Modules and sensors communicate to others and interact in normal operation. Refer to COMMUN/CA-
T/ONBETWEENMODULES THROUGH THE CAN BUSin this subsection.

Throttle Body Synchronization
Throttle bodies are precisely synchronized at the
factory. Replacement throttle bodies do not re-
quire synchronization to a specific engine.
NOTE: Under normal conditions, the ECM has
the ability to compensate for throttle body vari-
ations between both cylinders using the fuel
injection system.
Do not attempt to adjust the syn-
chronization screws on the throttle body. Any
tampering with the factory settings may result
in reduced engine efficiency.

Section 01 MAINTENANCE Subsection 01 (MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE)
MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE Maintenance is very important for keeping your trailer in safe operating condition: The mainte- nance schedule does not exempt the pre-ride inspection. Every year: Check coupler  condition and tighten coupler fasteners. Check tires condition and wear: Inspect wheels for damages. Check wheel bearing seals. Inspect lights for any damage and proper oper- ation: Check cover latches and cables including safety latch cable operation and lubricate cables if nec- essary. Lubricate key barrel using cable lube. Check tightness of frame fasteners. Every 12 000 km (7,500 mi): Verify and grease wheel hub bearings. Verify and grease coupler mechanism: Verify coupler safety cables condition:

XENON LIGHT KIT
Units with Xenon light kits installed Xenon kits may be tested before being installed, or failure may be diagnosed very easily after installa- tion. When installed, the normal light wires (rd-bl and bk) are extended down to the ballast boxes in- stalled behind the storage bin by the new harness. (see kit instructions) When the lights are to come on, the ballasts are powered up by the extended head- light wires. The ballasts are step-up transformers that convert the DC 12v to DC 1100 volts. (hence the warning labels) . Another extension wire, (HID Harness) runs from the ballasts back up to the head- lights to power the high intensity bulbs where a high voltage arc produces the light. The stock high beam wires connect directly to the headlight modules. The rdd2011-001-019 high beams are not different filaments but simply TYPYCAL BENCH TEST shutters that act as eye lids" inside the eye bulbs'
To test the lights: Unplug the 6 pin lighting connector just above the storage bin latch, (or bench test ) Use micro jumper wires to apply 12 Vdc to the RDIBL and BK male pins inside the connector: If one light does not light, check all connectors for "backed out' or damaged terminals. If connections appear ok, swap high voltage wires at the headlights from one lighting unit to the other: If the problem stays with the same light, suspect the lighting unit If the problem follows the high voltage wire, suspect the ballast unit, or power supply: By swapping known good components and connections, you will quickly identify the problem: Apply 12 Vdc to the GR and BK wires in the 6-pin connector to diagnose the high beam shutters: Simply listen for a loud click in each lighting unit, when voltage is applied.

STEERING ANGLE SENSOR (SAS) CODES
AII models This is an example of a list of codes that could appear if the wheels are not straight when the SAS is reset. Although all these codes relate to the SAS, the C0051 code is the one that caused the other codes. The C0051 code is triggered by a discrepancy be- tween the SAS and the YRS. If the vehicle is mov- ing straight ahead and SAS data shows a steering angle of + 2.0o or more while the YRS shows a 0 degree (straight) trajectory, the VCM will compare these values for a short distance then generate the above codes and put the vehicle in limp home mode. In order to resolve this, the wheels must be posi- tioned absolutely straight while the SAS is reset. The best way to do this is to reset the SAS while the handlebars are held in place during a complete wheel alignment procedure. Another method is to roll the vehicle back and forth in a straight line (as shown in Warranty Bulletin 2010 7) prior to resetting SAS. If the codes continue to reappear and you are sure of the accuracy of your reset procedure, the SAS should be replaced: It could take up to 30 miles (S0km) for the codes to appear; depending on the driving habits of the cus- tomer: Riding on straight roads for longer distances will trip the codes and put the unit into limp home mode sooner

CENTRIFUGAL CLUTCH OVERVIEW
AlI SES models The first SE5 models in 2008 and 2009 were equipped with the centrifugal clutch assembly (PIN 420 685 540) , which had 5 spring washers and 9 bushing type rollers. In some driving conditions the driver may experience creeping when the unit is at idle in Ist gear and the brake is released. In this circumstance the unit will move forward on its own: If the driver "blips" the throttle and the unit stops creeping, the centrifugal clutch is staying partially engaged: To remedy this symptom, (PIN 420 685 543) cen- trifugal clutch assembly was introduced as a replace ment part: It has 9 needle bearing type rollers to re- duce friction and fully disengage sooner: For 2010 RT and late production 2010 RS models there was a change in configuration for the rollers: These clutches were equipped with 6 needle bear- ing and 3 bushing type rollers. This combination could occasionally allow the  centrifugal clutch to stay slightly engaged and cause the unit to creep. In some instances the clutch would remain engaged enough to stall the engine. This was addressed with the release of warranty bulletin 2010-5. There were two other changes to the centrifugal clutch assembly beginning with the 2010 RT and late production 2010 RS models. The five conical spring washers used in the original versions (2008 early production 2010 GS/RS models) were replaced with a single flat wave washer: The center sleeve in both styles of clutch is identical in diameter and height: The difference between them is the circlip groove height. The circlip groove in the new style clutch is about mm lower than the previous version in order to increase spring preload on the single spring: The spring washer and wave washer style centrifugal clutch assemblies cannot be interchanged. In summary 2008-2009 GS and early production 2010 RS SES models use centrifugal clutch assembly (PIN 420 685 543). Late production 2010 RS and 2010 RT models use centrifugal clutch assembly (PIN 420 685 545.) Centrifugal Weight rollers: Rollers can be identified by looking at it's pin diam- eter: The pin on the bushing style roller is 6 mm in diameter and the bearing style pin diameter is 4.7 mm_ NOTE: Do not mix the old and the new rollers in a clutch: 2011 Technical Update Book Can-Am

TURN SIGNAL OPERATION AND DIAGNOSIS
2011 RT AII RT Models The turn signals are operated by the multifunction gauge. The multifunction gauge can either flash the left; the right or both: In addition, it cancels the turn signals. The switch inputs from the left multifunc- tion switch are received by the multifunction gauge. These switch inputs are not contact switches but are received by the gauge as CAN (Controller Area Net- work) signals and cannot be diagnosed using a mul- ti-meter: However; it is possible to use B.U.D.S. to diagnose the left hand multifunction switch buttons: The multifunction gauge interprets the CAN signals and is programmed to send a voltage signal to the turn signals and flash the lights. The turn signals will turn off automatically after a turn when the handlebars are returned to center: The multifunction gauge receives a CAN signal from the SAS (Steering Angle Sensor) to determine that the turn has been initiated and completed. However; af- ter a shallow turn or lane change the turn signal may be turned off manually or will automatically turn off after 30 seconds while the vehicle is moving straight ahead. If the vehicle is stationary, the turn signals will stay on untila turn is completed, the vehicle moves, they are turned OFF manually, or until the ignition key is switched OFF

New XPS 4 Stroke Oil Features The new second generation XPS oils are now available Make no mistake, the new XPS oils are in fact new oils and have been through an intensive development program to deliver the best oils ever offered from BRP There are cheaper oils offered from other company's, but keep in mind, all Rotax engines are developed along with BRP's XPS oils. There have been confirmed cases of engine failures related to the poor quality from other brand oils and BRP highly recommends the exclusive use of XPS oil. The newly developed second generation XPS oils will prove to be the best oils ever offered from BRP It can not be overstated how much research and development went into making the new XPS oil the best oil to work in conjunction with Rotax engines. AII Rotax engines ranging from lower output fan cooled engine, to high output liquid cooled 2 and 4 stroke engines have been tested in normal to extreme conditions with the new XPS oils. Without question the new 4 stroke XPS oils are the best oils available for all Rotax engines. Regardless of what oil brand a customer chooses, it is always best to drain down oil reservoirs before switching oils. This helps avoid potential compatibility issues such as "gelling" or "gumming". See the following for more information (excluding chemical make-up) on the 4 stroke XPS oils The new XPS 4 stroke oils are a tremendous leap forward in technology: Low quality 4 stroke oils, are often developed with old technology, designed exclusively for the automotive applications. These oils struggle to provide the long term protection against wear and deposits in the new smaller displacement; high revving and higher output recreational engines. Typical automotive packages also do not have adequate storage additives. The new XPS 4 stroke oils have additional corrosion inhibitors to protect recreational engines during extended storage periods due to seasonal use. These additives are state of the art; and fully protect internal engine components from corrosion: This is especially important for salty environments, humid environments, and moisture in the oil sump as a result of intermittent machine use. One of the most important features of the new XPS 4 stroke synthetic formula is the improved Viscosity Index (VI). An engine using the new XPS 4 stoke oil starts easier in cold temperatures and stays at the proper operating viscosity in hot temperatures: Because of this technology, there is a much wider operating range with optimum engine protection in extreme temperatures. The latest on liquid oil engineering technologies and development are integrated into the new XPS oil formulations, combined with a tremendous amount of testing in order to ensure that the next generation of BRP oils are fit for the next generations of BRP engines.

Occurred Fault Codes An occurred fault code indicates a fault that was active, but no longer is, The occurred fault does not presently affect sys- tem or component operation but is retained as a history of the faults that were detected_ Inactive Fault Codes An inactive fault code represents a fault code that is neither active , nor occurred.
